**Rohit Gurunath Sharma – Overview**

- **Born:** 30 April 1987, Nagpur, Maharashtra, India  
- **Role:** Right‑handed top‑order batter; occasional right‑arm off‑spin bowler  
- **Domestic Teams:** Mumbai (Ranji Trophy), Mumbai Indians (Indian Premier League)  
- **International Teams:** India national cricket team (all formats)  

---

### Early Life & Domestic Career
- Grew up in a cricket‑loving family; his father, Gurunath Sharma, was a former cricketer for Vidarbha.  
- Made his first‑class debut for **Mumbai** in 2006, quickly establishing himself as a prolific run‑scorer in the Ranji Trophy.  
- Joined the **Mumbai Indians** (MI) in the inaugural IPL season (2008) and later became the side’s captain, leading MI to five IPL titles (2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2020).

---

### International Career Highlights
| Format | Debut | Major Tournaments Won | Notable Achievements |
|--------|-------|-----------------------|----------------------|
| **ODI** | 23 Oct 2007 vs. Australia | 2007 T20 World Cup, 2013 ICC Champions Trophy, 2024 T20 World Cup, 2025 ICC Champions Trophy | Holds the world record for the highest individual ODI score (264 runs). First player to hit three double‑centuries in ODIs. Most centuries in Cricket World Cups (7). |
| **T20I** | 12 Jun 2007 vs. England | 2007 T20 World Cup, 2024 T20 World Cup | Joint record for most T20I centuries (5). Most runs in T20 Internationals. |
| **Test** | 6 Nov 2013 vs. West Indies | — | Consistent opening batsman, contributing crucial centuries in overseas conditions. |

- **Captaincy:** Served as India’s captain across all three formats, becoming the first and only player to lead a side in every ICC tournament final. Under his leadership India won the **2024 T20 World Cup**, the **2025 ICC Champions Trophy**, the **2018 & 2023 Asia Cups** (ODI format), and the **2018 Nidahas Trophy** (T20I).

---

### Record‑Breaking Performances
- **Highest ODI Score:** 264 runs vs. Sri Lanka (2014) – the highest individual total in any ODI.  
- **Double Centuries:** Three ODI double‑hundreds (209, 264, 250*).  
- **World Cup Centuries:** Seven centuries across Cricket World Cups, the most by any player.  
- **T20I Centuries:** Five centuries, sharing the record for most in the format.  
- **Sixes:** Holds the record for most sixes in international cricket (across ODIs, T20Is, and Tests).  
- **Runs:** All‑time leader in runs scored in T20 Internationals.

---

### Awards & Honours
| Year | Award | Reason |
|------|-------|--------|
| **2015** | **Arjuna Award** | Outstanding performance in cricket. |
| **2020** | **Khel Ratna Award** | India’s highest sporting honour for his contributions and leadership. |
| **2026** | **Padma Shri** | Fourth‑highest civilian award, recognizing his long‑standing impact on Indian cricket, including the 2024 T20 World Cup triumph. |
| **2019** | **ICC Men’s ODI Cricketer of the Year** | For his record‑breaking World Cup performances. |

---

### Leadership & Influence
- **IPL Success:** Captained Mumbai Indians to five IPL titles, tying with MS Dhoni for the most championships as a captain.  
- **International Leadership:** Guided India to historic victories, notably becoming the **second Indian captain** to win a T20 World Cup (2024) and the **first Indian captain** to win two T20 World Cups.  
- **Consistency:** One of only two players to have featured in every edition of the T20 World Cup from its inception in 2007 through 2024.

---

### Playing Style & Reputation
- **Batting:** Renowned for a smooth, elegant technique combined with explosive power. Excels as an opening batsman in limited‑overs cricket, capable of building innings and accelerating at will.  
- **Fielding:** Agile and reliable, often positioned in the inner circle.  
- **Leadership:** Praised for calm decision‑making, strategic acumen, and the ability to inspire teammates in high‑pressure situations.  

---

### Off‑Field Presence
- **Social Media:** Active on Instagram (@rohitsharma45) with a massive following, using the platform to engage fans and promote charitable initiatives.  
- **Philanthropy:** Involved in various charitable activities, especially those promoting sports among underprivileged children.

---

### Summary
Rohit Sharma stands out as one of the most accomplished modern cricketers, combining prolific run‑scoring, record‑setting performances, and successful captaincy. His contributions have earned him a place among cricket’s greats, reflected in numerous individual records, multiple major tournament victories, and prestigious national honours. His influence extends beyond the field through leadership, mentorship, and a strong public presence.

sources.snippet: Rohit Gurunath Sharma (born 30 April 1987) is an Indian international cricketer and the former captain of the India national cricket team in all formats of the game. He is a right-handed top-order batter. He represents Mumbai in domestic cricket and Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League. Sharma was a member of the teams that won the 2007 T20 World Cup, the 2013 ICC Champions Trophy and was the winning captain of the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy. Sharma is widely regarded as a modern-day great, known for his leadership and explosive batting.Sharma holds several batting records which include most runs in T20 Internationals, most sixes in international cricket, most double centuries in ODI cricket (three), most centuries at Cricket World Cups (seven) and joint most centuries in Twenty20 Internationals (five). He also holds the world record for the highest individual score (264) in a One Day International (ODI) and also holds the record for scoring most centuries (five) in a single Cricket World Cup, for which he won the ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year award in 2019. He is the first and only captain to lead a team in all ICC tournament finals.He formerly captained Mumbai Indians and the team has won five Indian Premier League titles in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020 under him, making him the most successful captain in IPL history, sharing this record with MS Dhoni. He is also one of two players who have played in every edition of the T20 World Cup, from the inaugural edition in 2007 till 2024. He is the only Indian player to win two T20 World Cups. He became the second Indian captain to win a T20 World Cup.He has received three national honours, the Arjuna Award in 2015, the prestigious Khel Ratna Award in 2020 by the Government of India, and the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in 2026, for his immense, long standing contribution to Indian cricket, which notably includes leading India to victory in the 2024 T20 World Cup and the 2025 ICC Champions Trophy. Under his captaincy, India also won the 2018 Asia Cup and the 2023 Asia Cup, the seventh and eighth time the country won the title, both in ODI format as well as the 2018 Nidahas Trophy, their second overall and first in T20I format.

content: what does the bengaluru.xlsx is about

**Bengaluru.xlsx** is an Excel workbook that belongs to the **WatchCovidly** project on GitHub.  
The file is intended to help users “read closely” and identify **sensitive areas in Bengaluru where people have been placed under quarantine by the Government of Karnataka**.  

Key points about the workbook:

- **Purpose** – It serves as a data source for tracking COVID‑19‑related quarantine zones within the city.  
- **Content** – While the exact columns are not listed in the snippet, such files typically include information such as:
  - Names or identifiers of the quarantine areas  
  - Geographic details (e.g., neighborhoods, coordinates, or postal codes)  
  - Dates when quarantine orders were issued or lifted  
  - Possibly the number of cases or the status of each zone  
- **Context** – The workbook is part of the **WatchCovidly** repository, which aggregates and visualizes COVID‑19 data for Karnataka. The repository’s description emphasizes that the file helps users “know the sensitive areas where people are put in quarantine.”  

In summary, **Bengaluru.xlsx** is a data set used by the WatchCovidly application to map and monitor quarantine‑designated locations in Bengaluru, providing a reference for authorities, researchers, or the public to understand where COVID‑19 containment measures are in effect.

content: what is this is about YC_Bengaluru_Companies.xlsx (.XLSX)

The file is a spreadsheet that lists Y Combinator‑backed companies based in Bengaluru.  

It includes a “How to use this sheet” guide that explains the columns:

* **Column E – YC Profile URL** – automatically generated from the company name using the standard Y Combinator URL pattern (`ycombinator.com/companies/<company‑name>`).  
* **Column F – Career Page Link** – left blank for you to fill in after visiting each company’s Y Combinator profile and copying its jobs or external careers page.  
* **Column G – Applied** – a checkbox you can use to track which companies you’ve applied to.  
* **Column H – Notes** – free‑form space for referral contacts, role applied for, status, etc.  

The sheet also contains rows of company data (ID, name, short description, batch, YC profile link, and the three blank columns mentioned above). It is intended to help you organize job‑search outreach to Bengaluru‑based YC companies.
